sum: Global pressure on China’s rare earth exports has moved from background noise to front-page risk, and supply chains linked to defense, EVs and electronics now sit under a much harsher spotlight. That stress can punish exposed stocks or reward companies that help keep critical minerals flowing. This article walks through three stocks from the Non-Chinese Critical-Minerals and Rare-Earth Supply Chain Enablers screener that appear positively exposed to the latest US China trade flare up.

The three stocks in focus are only a sample of what this theme captures, as the full screen flags 9 more companies with rare earth or critical mineral angles that could matter just as much to supply chain resilience as the ones covered below. To see the broader field and start sorting for your own highest conviction ideas, head into the Non-Chinese Critical-Minerals and Rare-Earth Supply Chain Enablers screener to identify, filter, and analyze potential Non-Chinese Critical-Minerals and Rare-Earth Supply Chain Enablers aligned with your approach.

Shin-Etsu Chemical is a Japanese materials giant that fits this ex China critical-minerals theme through its electronic materials and rare earth magnet products supporting semiconductor and advanced industrial supply chains. It generates about ¥1.1t from electronic materials, ¥1.0t from infrastructure and ¥478b from functional materials, with a market cap near ¥9.6t.

For investors focused on non Chinese critical-minerals routes, Shin-Etsu Chemical offers scale, rare earth related products and a broad role in semiconductor and electronics supply that could gain relevance if supply chains keep shifting away from China, especially if one unseen pressure on pricing power breaks in its favor.

REalloys is a pure-play North American rare earth metals producer supplying elements like neodymium, dysprosium, terbium, samarium, gadolinium, yttrium and scandium for defense, electronics and EV supply chains, with all reported revenue of about $2 million from Metals & Mining and a market value near $404 million.

REalloys offers direct, non-Chinese rare earth exposure at the materials level. Its mine to magnet ambition is closely tied to US efforts to secure supply for defense, EV and electronics manufacturing.

sum: If Orbia Advance Corporation. de sat on your watchlist instead of in your account this year, the outcome may feel expensive. Investors who held Orbia Advance Corporation. de from the start of the year are up 43.6%, including dividends. That move arrived while bulls and bears argued over whether heavy spending on new plants and advanced materials would actually pay. The key question is simple. How could you have judged, back in January 2026, whether those expansion plans would really translate into stronger earnings power?
The easy part of this move is behind Orbia Advance Corporation. de. Zero in on 199 high quality undervalued stocks for companies trading below our estimates.
The Argument You Would Have Been Weighing On Orbia Advance Corporation. de
The shares cost MX$15.59 at the start of the period, and anyone looking at Orbia Advance Corporation. de then had to choose between two very different stories about the same business.

The bullish view pointed to heavy investment paying off, with a Fair Value of MX$27.84, a rough guide to what that script said the stock could be worth if things played out. That camp leaned on new facilities and advanced materials tied to infrastructure, energy storage, and digital connectivity demand.

The bearish Narrative saw rising ESG compliance costs and overcapacity as the real anchor, with a Fair Value of MX$10.96 built on that harsher picture. That side focused on regulatory pressure on plastics, competition from sustainable alternatives, and leverage staying above 3x net debt to EBITDA.

items.t: L'Air Liquide S.A. (AIQUF) Stock Price, News, Quote & History
sum: L'Air Liquide S.A. provides gases, technologies, and services for the industrial and health sectors in Europe, the Americas, the Asia Pacific, the Middle East, and Africa. It operates in Gas & Services, and Engineering & Construction segments. The Gas & Services segment comprises large industries business, which offers gas and energy solutions including oxygen, nitrogen, argon, hydrogen, and carbon monoxide, as well as operates cogeneration plants to supply steam and electricity to metals, chemicals, refining, and energy industries; and industrial merchant business line provides industrial gases, equipment, hardgoods, and associated services to materials and energy, materials and chemicals, food and pharmaceuticals, technology and research, and fabrication and construction sectors. This segment also includes healthcare business, which provides medical gases, home healthcare services, medical equipment, and specialty ingredient; healthcare professionals, and hospitals; and electronic business supply carrier gases, electronic specialty and advanced materials, equipment and installation, service, and analysis to semiconductor, flat panel, and photovoltaic markets. The Engineering & Construction segment designs, develops, and builds industrial gas production plants to third parties; and designs and manufacture plants in the traditional, renewable, and alternative energy sectors. This segment also focuses on markets which require a global approach, drawing on science, technologies, development models, and usages related to digital transformation. L'Air Liquide S.A. was incorporated in 1902 and is headquartered in Paris, France.

Citizen diplomacy brings Korea, Japan closer
sum: When you are abroad, you will more often than not find yourself becoming a patriot. Older Koreans say people tend to develop a greater sense of unity and solidarity with their community when they live in a foreign country. Their shared sense of identity often brings them closer together and helps them maintain a strong bond.
It is common to see Koreans gather to share happiness, guided by the belief that happiness doubles and sorrow is halved when shared with others.

Compared with this sense of unity among people of the same ethnic background, it is relatively uncommon to see people from a different culture throw a party solely to celebrate the achievements of a Korean. The chances are even slimmer when the host is Japanese, given the two countries' long and often contentious history.
Such a rare event took place in Houston, Texas, in September.

Akemi Saitoh, the wife of Yasuhiko Saitoh, president of Japan's largest chemical company Shin-Etsu, invited some 70 guests — most of them people of Korean descent — to their Houston residence on Sept. 20 for a party celebrating Korean ballerina Kim Danbi. Kim was promoted to principal dancer at Houston Ballet in June.
There was more good news for Kim. The City of Houston proclaimed Sept. 20, 2026, as Danbi Kim Day in recognition of her accomplishments since she joined the renowned ballet company in 2018.

“I admire what she has accomplished,” Saitoh told The Korea Times. “Becoming a principal dancer is an extraordinary achievement, and I have so much respect for the dedication it takes to reach that position.”

Japan's Nikkei rebounds after 3 days, closes at 66,753 on semiconductor-led gains; September marks second straight monthly rise
sum: The Nikkei Stock Average rebounded on the Tokyo stock market on September 30, closing up 1,272.45 yen (1.94%) from the previous day at 66,753.72, snapping a three-session losing streak. The close marked the highest level since August 18. Following gains in U.S. semiconductor-related stocks the previous day, buying spread across a broad range of issues in Tokyo from the morning session. The index extended its gains in the afternoon, rising as much as 1,464 yen at one point.

The Nikkei opened 0.99% higher, and while momentum stalled in mid-morning trading, the upward trend strengthened again in the afternoon. After dipping below the 65,000 level during the previous session, the market had pared losses on probe buying by overseas investors. With the subsequent recovery, overseas speculative funds grew increasingly bullish on the near-term outlook, expanding their purchases of stock index futures. SoftBank Group (9984.T), a heavy contributor to the index, surged more than 6%, while Fast Retailing also climbed further.

In the U.S. market the previous day, the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX), which tracks major chip-related stocks, rose more than 1%. Carrying that momentum into Tokyo, buying was concentrated in semiconductor names such as Tokyo Electron (8035.T) and Advantest (6857.T). Even amid persistently high interest rates in both Japan and the U.S., expectations for strong earnings growth continued to attract capital into semiconductor-related stocks. Bank shares, which tend to benefit from higher rates, were also bought back.

The Tokyo Stock Price Index (TOPIX) also rebounded after three sessions, closing up 67.52 points (1.67%) at 4,108.65. On the Tokyo Stock Exchange Prime Market, advancing issues numbered 1,127, accounting for roughly 70% of the total, while decliners totaled 368 and 55 were unchanged. Trading value reached approximately ¥9.1212 trillion (approximately $57.8 billion), with trading volume of 2.76231 billion shares.

Among individual stocks, Taiyo Yuden (6976.T) and TDK (6762.T) were firm. The two companies announced on September 29 a business alliance to jointly develop next-generation electronic components, which was well received by investors. Taiyo Yuden surged sharply at one point.

items.t: Shin-Etsu Chemical Plunges as Full-Year Outlook Misses ¥760 Billion Market Forecast; Chugai Pharmaceutical Also Disappoints
sum: On Monday the 27th, the Tokyo stock market saw a stark divergence in the performance of major companies that reported quarterly earnings the previous weekend. Shin-Etsu Chemical (4063.T) and Chugai Pharmaceutical (4519.T) both fell sharply, while select information services and airline sector stocks attracted buying interest.

Shin-Etsu Chemical shares extended their decline sharply, falling ¥556 from the previous weekend's close to ¥6,146. The company's first-quarter (April-June) results for the fiscal year ending March 2027 showed operating profit rose 4.2% year-on-year to ¥173.8 billion (approximately $1.1 billion), roughly in line with market expectations. However, the company maintained its full-year operating profit forecast at ¥700 billion (approximately $4.3 billion), up 10.2% from the previous fiscal year, which disappointed investors. The figure significantly undershoots the market consensus of around ¥760 billion (approximately $4.6 billion), triggering selling driven by disappointment.

While supply and demand for semiconductor silicon wafers remain tight, the outlook for the living environment and infrastructure materials segment—including subsidiary Shin-Etsu Polymer, which handles polyvinyl chloride resin—is seen as more cautious than the market had anticipated, contributing to the earnings forecast falling short of expectations.

Chugai Pharmaceutical also fell sharply in a significant pullback, ending the session at ¥6,848, down ¥568 from the previous weekend. The company's core operating profit for the second quarter (April-June) of the fiscal year ending December 2026 was ¥165.9 billion (approximately $1.0 billion), up 25.2% year-on-year, but appeared to miss market estimates by about 5%. Cumulative first-half (January-June) results totaled ¥329.1 billion (approximately $2.0 billion), putting the run rate slightly below 50% of the full-year forecast of ¥670 billion (approximately $4.1 billion).

Market observers attributed Chugai Pharmaceutical's earnings shortfall to lower-than-expected sales of the hemophilia treatment Hemlibra to Swiss pharmaceutical giant Roche, as well as royalty income from the oral obesity treatment Foundayo remaining at low levels.

items.t: Disco Plunges, KOA Surges as Semiconductor Stocks Diverge; SoftBank Group Also Slides
sum: The Tokyo stock market on the 24th saw active stock-picking driven by earnings announcements and forecast revisions. In the semiconductor sector, a stark contrast emerged as Disco (6146.T) plunged while KOA (6999.T) surged. SoftBank Group (9984.T) also fell sharply, pressured by heightened caution over AI investment that swept through the U.S. market.

Disco, a major semiconductor manufacturing equipment maker, plunged ¥8,520 (12.3%) to ¥60,890. While the company reported first-quarter operating profit rose 42.2% year-on-year to ¥49 billion (approximately $299.1 million), its July-September plan of ¥55.9 billion (approximately $341.2 million) fell short of the market consensus of just over ¥60 billion, souring sentiment. Although this was seen as consistent with the company's tendency to set conservative plans, the broader weakness in semiconductor stocks that day added headwinds, leading to heavy selling.

In contrast, electronic components manufacturer KOA surged ¥288 (11.5%) to ¥2,782. First-quarter operating profit jumped 70.2% year-on-year to ¥850 million (approximately $5.2 million), a significant increase. Demand for industrial and AI-related equipment in Japan, China, and other Asian regions, as well as industrial equipment demand in Europe, proved stronger than expected. The company sharply raised its full-year operating profit forecast from ¥2.83 billion to ¥5.36 billion (approximately $17.3 million to $32.7 million) and its annual dividend from ¥39 to ¥63 per share.

Shin-Etsu Polymer (7970.T), which specializes in precision molded products, extended its sharp decline, falling ¥220 (8.9%) to ¥2,257. First-quarter operating profit rose 8.6% year-on-year to ¥4.15 billion (approximately $25.3 million), and the company forecast full-year profit of ¥16 billion (approximately $97.6 million), up 14.0% year-on-year. However, the outlook merely met market consensus, and the lack of positive surprises led to selling pressure. The company plans an annual dividend of ¥66 per share, up ¥4 from the previous year.
SoftBank Group fell sharply, dropping ¥418 (7.1%) to ¥5,500.

Nikkei 225 Plunges Over 1,700 Points, Breaks Below 65,000 on U.S. Tech Rout and Middle East Risks
sum: Japan's Nikkei 225 Stock Average suffered a sharp reversal on July 24, with intraday losses exceeding 1,700 points from the previous close. The index plunged decisively below the 65,000 threshold shortly after the opening bell, trading around the 64,800 level at times. The sell-off directly tracked the prior day's U.S. market rout, where major indices fell led by technology stocks, prompting foreign investors to aggressively dump index futures and core artificial intelligence-related names in Tokyo.

The Nikkei opened at 65,584.25, down 838.35 points from the previous close, before accelerating its decline. The broader TOPIX also reversed course, briefly dipping below the 4,000 mark. On July 23, U.S. markets extended their slide, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average falling 506.93 points to 51,711.65 and the Nasdaq Composite tumbling 553.20 points to 25,137.70. Earnings reports from Alphabet (GOOG) and Tesla (TSLA) reignited concerns about excessive investment in AI, while a warning from U.S. President Trump about a large-scale attack on Iran stoked fears of rising crude oil prices, rapidly chilling investor sentiment.

Adding to the pressure, solid U.S. employment data released the same day pushed up the probability of Federal Reserve rate hikes within the year, with rate-hike jitters further weighing on the market. In Japan, crude oil futures and U.S. long-term yields rose against the backdrop of escalating Middle East tensions. Japanese long-term yields also firmed, making equities appear relatively overvalued.

Among individual stocks, selling was broad-based, particularly in high-priced semiconductor and AI-related names. Among the most actively traded issues by value, major tech stocks fell across the board, including Disco (6146.T), SoftBank Group (9984.T), Advantest (6857.T), Tokyo Electron (8035.T), Kioxia Holdings (285A.T), Fanuc (6954.T), Murata Manufacturing (6981.T), and Shin-Etsu Chemical (4063.T). Selling was particularly pronounced in heavily index-weighted stocks such as SoftBank Group and Advantest.
Airline stocks also fell sharply amid the crude oil surge, with selling spreading across a wide range of sectors including non-ferrous metals, services, rubber products, and chemicals.

items.t: Nikkei 225 Plunges Over 2,000 Points, Breaches 65,000 as AI and Semiconductor Stocks Get Crushed
sum: The Nikkei 225 suffered a severe extended decline on the Tokyo Stock Exchange on July 17, with losses briefly topping 2,000 points. After opening at 66,339.85, down 495.69 points from the previous day, selling pressure showed no signs of abating, pushing the index below the psychologically important 65,000 threshold. This marks the first time the Nikkei has fallen below 65,000 since June 12, roughly one month ago.

In the U.S. market on July 16, the June Producer Price Index (PPI) fell 0.3% month-over-month, easing inflation concerns. However, the Dow Jones Industrial Average and the Nasdaq Composite both snapped a two-day winning streak to close lower. Weakness in the semiconductor sector was particularly pronounced, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX) declining, a trend that the Tokyo market inherited directly. From the morning session, stocks perceived as artificial intelligence (AI) and semiconductor plays were hit with intermittent waves of selling.

The settlement price for Nikkei 225 futures (yen-denominated) on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) came in at 66,040, down 800 points from the Osaka Exchange settlement price on July 16, already setting a heavy tone for the physical market. This weakness in futures chilled investor sentiment even before the opening bell.

The selling was concentrated in major AI and semiconductor-related stocks that had previously led the broader market rally. Semiconductor manufacturing equipment names such as Advantest (6857.T), Tokyo Electron (8035.T), and Disco (6146.T) suffered significant declines in the machinery and electric appliances sectors. In the non-ferrous metals sector, Fujikura (5803.T) and Sumitomo Electric Industries (5802.T), which had attracted attention for wire and cable demand related to AI data centers, were sold off. The chemical sector also saw weakness, with Resonac Holdings (4004.T) and Shin-Etsu Chemical (4063.T) trading lower. In the information and communications sector, SoftBank Group (9984.T) declined. Kioxia (285A.T), the major semiconductor memory maker that had just listed the previous day, was also pushed lower by selling.
Across industry sectors, a broad-based sell-off intensified.

sum: The Nikkei 225 rebounded on the 15th, closing at 67,743.50, up 500.77 points (0.74%) from the previous day. The Tokyo market opened lower, extending the sell-off in U.S. tech stocks from the prior session, but bargain-hunting in semiconductor-related names gained momentum in the afternoon, pushing the index into positive territory. A recovery in South Korea's KOSPI and easing crude oil prices also underpinned investor sentiment, with the benchmark finishing near its session high.

Advantest (6857.T), the semiconductor testing equipment giant, was the top point contributor, single-handedly lifting the Nikkei 225 by approximately 230 points. The company's shares surged 955 yen to close at 29,775 yen. Alongside Advantest, SoftBank Group (9984.T) contributed roughly 168 points and Kioxia Holdings (285A.T) added about 46 points, with these three stocks alone accounting for the bulk of the index's advance.

Market breadth on the Tokyo Stock Exchange's Prime Market was overwhelmingly positive, with 176 issues advancing, 47 declining, and 2 unchanged — 76% of all stocks ended higher. Trading volume reached 2.402 billion shares, with turnover totaling ¥10.76 trillion (approximately $66.3 billion), reflecting active participation.

By sector, mining, shipping, and chemicals led the advance, while non-ferrous metals, machinery, and glass and ceramics products declined. Beyond Advantest and SoftBank Group, top positive contributors included Kioxia Holdings, Recruit Holdings (6098.T), Shin-Etsu Chemical (4063.T), Nitto Denko (6988.T), and TDK (6762.T).

On the downside, Fast Retailing (9983.T) was the heaviest drag, shaving approximately 115 points off the Nikkei 225. The stock tumbled 1,440 yen to close at 79,790 yen. Other notable decliners included Ibiden (4062.T), Fujikura (5803.T), Fanuc (6954.T), Yaskawa Electric (6506.T), and Tokyo Electron (8035.T).

In the previous U.S. session, a decline in SK Hynix — the South Korean memory chipmaker that listed on the Nasdaq last week — weighed on the broader tech sector. Crude oil prices also climbed after President Trump declared the resumption of a blockade on Iranian vessels in the Strait of Hormuz.

High-purity materials used in these fabrication steps tend to benefit significantly from trends such as increased memory stacking and production volume expansion. Its year-to-date price change exceeds +180%.

It provides supply systems for specialty gases and chemicals, piping installation, operational management, and maintenance services to semiconductor fabs. Demand arises during new fab construction or production line expansions, and a key strength is its ability to generate recurring revenue from maintenance and management services after plant operations begin. If Kioxia enhances its production capacity, this company could benefit from associated fab infrastructure investments. Its stock has risen over 70% year-to-date.

The company specializes in optimization technologies that accelerate software development and enhance processing performance in storage, image processing, and AI systems. It also has strong expertise in quantum technologies.

SESA’s 14,000-square-foot, state-of-the-art Cosmetics Application Laboratory is located 20 miles from Manhattan and Newark International Airport, allowing for SESA to be closer to many of its strategic customers based in New York and New Jersey.

Silicone Elastomer Gel (INCI: C13-15 Alkane (and) Dimethicone/Vinyl Dimethicone Crosspolymer) is a non-emulsifying elastomer gel with superior oil thickening control capability. The unique silicone gel consists of silicone crosspolymer and natural derived hydrocarbon. Notably, it is an effective thickening agent for low viscosity silicone and organic oils–providing a silky, dry, smooth feeling on the skin. The gel can be used across a variety of cosmetic applications.

Alkyl/Polyglycerin Co-modified Silicone Elastomer Gel (INCI: Coco-Caprylate/Caprate (and) Lauryl Dimethicone/Polyglycerin-3 Crosspolymer) is an alkyl chain-modified silicone gel emulsifier that is combined with a natural origin oil. items.t: A-Shares Mixed at Midday: Shanghai Composite Drops 1%, STAR 50 Rallies Over 1%; Hong Kong Tech Stocks Surge
sum: China's A-share market displayed significant structural divergence during the morning session on July 7. While the three major indices declined collectively—with the Shanghai Composite Index briefly extending its intraday loss to 1%—the STAR Board, represented by the semiconductor supply chain, showed robust strength, with the STAR 50 Index rallying over 1% against the trend. Meanwhile, sentiment in the Hong Kong market warmed up, with the Hang Seng Tech Index surging more than 2% driven by large-cap internet stocks, forming a stark contrast with the weakness in traditional heavyweight sectors on the A-share market.

Near the midday close, the core market indices stood as follows: the Shanghai Composite fell 0.89%, the Shenzhen Component dropped 0.70%, and the ChiNext Index declined 0.60%. The Shanghai Composite briefly touched a 1% loss around 10:34 AM, while the ChiNext Index turned negative after a brief early-session spike into positive territory, with its loss reaching 0.9% at one point. Petrochemical, shipping, pharmaceutical, and precious metals sectors were the primary drags on the broader market.

In stark contrast to the weakness on the main board, the STAR 50 Index surged over 1% against the trend, with the semiconductor supply chain becoming the core focus of capital inflows. Sub-sectors including semiconductor silicon wafers, ASIC chips, and the broader semiconductor industry all saw significant rallies. Meanwhile, concept stocks such as lab-grown diamonds and online gaming were also active, while cyclical sectors like coal and petrochemicals fell into correction.

In Hong Kong, the market opened lower but staged a strong recovery. The Hang Seng Index opened down 0.2%, and the Hang Seng Tech Index opened 0.37% lower, but both quickly recovered lost ground and pushed aggressively higher. The Hang Seng Tech Index surged more than 2% intraday, with large-cap internet stocks leading the rebound. Meituan (03690.HK) rallied over 7% at one point, Tencent Holdings (00700.HK) gained more than 5%, and stocks such as Xiaomi Corporation (01810.HK), Lenovo Group (00992.HK), and Li Auto (02015.HK) all rose over 3%.

sum: The Nikkei 225 extended its winning streak to a third consecutive session on July 1, closing at 70,474.96, up 412.64 points, or 0.59%, from the previous trading day. Riding the momentum from a strong performance by U.S. tech stocks in the prior session, buying interest centered on semiconductor-related and electronic component names in the Tokyo market. Investor sentiment was also underpinned by the Bank of Japan's Tankan survey (June survey), released before the market open, which showed an improvement in the business conditions diffusion index (DI) for large manufacturers. However, after briefly approaching the 72,000 level in early trading, the index was pushed back by short-term profit-taking, trimming its intraday gains.

Trading volume on the Tokyo Stock Exchange Prime Market reached 2.27493 billion shares, with trading value totaling ¥10.4435 trillion (approximately $64.7 billion). By sector, metal products, electrical machinery, and machinery posted gains, while non-ferrous metals, shipping, and real estate declined. Advancing issues numbered 96, representing 43% of the total, while declining issues totaled 127, or 53%—a market where decliners outnumbered advancers, in contrast to the rise in the headline index.

The biggest contributor to the Nikkei's advance was Tokyo Electron (8035.T), which single-handedly added approximately 165 points to the index. The stock surged ¥1,650 to ¥78,800. Ibiden (4062.T) followed with a contribution of approximately 132 points, while Taiyo Yuden (6976.T) added about 83 points, Kyocera (6971.T) contributed roughly 69 points, and TDK (6762.T) added about 65 points, with electronic component and semiconductor-related names dominating the top contributor list.

Silicon Wafer Price Hikes Sweep the Industry: AI Demand Multiplier and Expiring Long-Term Contracts Open a Critical Window for China's Domestic Substitution
sum: In the summer of 2026, the silicon wafer segment—the most upstream link in the semiconductor industry chain—has finally welcomed a long-overdue wave of price increases. In June, leading Chinese wafer manufacturer Lion Micro was the first to announce a 10% to 15% price increase effective July 1. Almost simultaneously, three international giants—Japan's Shin-Etsu Chemical, Japan's SUMCO, and Taiwan's GlobalWafers—raised their 12-inch wafer quotations in tandem, with high-end specialty wafers tailored for artificial intelligence (AI) and high-performance computing (HPC) applications seeing even steeper increases of 18% to 22%.

This seemingly sudden wave of price adjustments is, in reality, a concentrated eruption of long-accumulated market supply-demand tensions. After enduring a deep downturn from 2023 to 2024 and the "darkest hour" of industry-wide losses in 2025, the silicon wafer sector is now reclaiming its pricing power within the semiconductor chain, fueled by the expiration of numerous low-price LTSAs and an explosion in downstream AI computing demand.

Understanding the current revival of the silicon wafer industry requires revisiting the heavy legacy of the last cycle. The 2021-2022 semiconductor super-cycle propelled silicon wafer prices to historic highs. The registration-based IPO system reform on China's STAR Market, combined with local government industrial support policies, led to a flood of new capacity entering the sector. However, beginning in 2023, the industry took a sharp downturn into a destocking cycle, with silicon wafer prices falling to roughly 60% of their previous peak. The brutal reality of this asset-heavy industry is that utilization rates directly dictate gross margins; many silicon wafer companies saw their gross margins plummet from highs of 20% to 40% in 2021 into negative territory.
To lock in customers and maintain cash flow during the trough, many silicon wafer manufacturers were forced to sign three-year LTSAs with downstream wafer foundries, fixing prices at the bottom.
